#Using Biblion in a Web Browser (Standalone Mode)

Product: Biblion Citation Assistant

Audience: Academic Researchers, Scientists & Medical Writers

Maintained by: Documentation Writer

#1. What Is Standalone Mode?

Biblion works in two places:

  • Inside Microsoft Word, as a taskpane add-in, where it can insert citations straight into your manuscript.
  • In any web browser, as a standalone app. Use it to search PubMed, read abstracts, organise your library and copy citations into any editor.

Biblion detects where it is running and adjusts itself.

#2. What Changes Outside Word

FeatureIn WordIn a browser
PubMed search, abstractsYesYes
My Library, collections, notes, exportYesYes
Cloud sync, account, billingYesYes
Insert Citation buttonYesReplaced by Copy Citation
Citation style selectorYesHidden
Live References tabYesHidden

#3. Copy a Citation in the Browser

  1. Search for an article.
  2. On its card, click Copy Citation. The button briefly changes to Copied!
  3. Paste into your document. You get the in-text citation and the full reference entry, formatted in the current style (APA 7th Edition by default in a browser).

#4. Works in a Narrow Taskpane Too

The layout adapts to narrow windows, down to about 320 px wide, the width of a typical Word taskpane. The header, the navigation and the search box stay usable.

#5. Navigating Biblion

The main navigation has three places:

  • Search: PubMed / MEDLINE search (home page)
  • My Library: your saved articles
  • About & Support: help, documentation guides, contact information

The footer links to the Privacy Policy and Terms of Use.
